title: NavigationMovement
description: What a NavigationAgentComponent needs from whatever moves its actor: an agent decides where to go next, its movement decides how the motion happens - through a physics world, by writing a node position, or anything else. While navigating, an agent calls move once in every fixed step it runs in, and stop once when it stops steering: on arrival, when the destination turns out unreachable, on NavigationAgentComponent.stop and when it is disabled. A step without a call means there is nothing to ask for. Directions are in the navigation space's coordinates, the same space an agent reads its position in. A movement working in another space - a projected display, say - converts at its own boundary. `KinematicMovementComponent` from `@codexo/exojs-physics` satisfies this contract as it is.

members.name: move
members.signature: move(direction: Readonly<PointLike>, distance: number, step: Seconds): void
members.description: Requests motion for the fixed step step that is being processed, along direction - a unit vector from an agent - and over no more than distance in total until the next request. An agent passes the distance to its destination on the last stretch and Infinity before it, so a movement that keeps applying a request for longer than one step - such as a physics world stepped several times per call - still stops on the destination. Called from an agent's fixed update, so the motion can still be applied within the same step.

members.name: stop
members.description: Ends the motion: the actor should come to rest.

members.name: maxSpeed
members.description: Distance per second that a direction of length 1 covers. An agent reads it to tell how far one step reaches, which decides when it turns toward the next waypoint and how much progress to expect.
